tone_patterns: Formal, role-centric governance tone emphasizing accountability and oversight
Uses precise, compliance-oriented language (e.g., oversight, approval, reporting lines, risk appetite) without promotional phrasing
Balances strategic governance framing (culture, agenda-setting) with operational execution framing (framework implementation, monitoring)
Employs authoritative verbs to describe responsibilities (responsible for, oversees, ensures, reviews, recommends, reports)
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short subsection heading naming a governance topic (role/committee) followed by a compact explanatory paragraph
Uses multi-paragraph blocks that progress from: (1) mandate/purpose, (2) responsibilities and interfaces, (3) integration into broader governance processes
Includes role biographies presented as structured narrative: experience summary → areas of expertise → external affiliations (if any) → internal responsibilities and governance contributions
Uses bridging sentences to connect roles (e.g., collaboration between sustainability and risk functions) and to show how topics flow across management levels
Employs bullet lists to enumerate commitments/targets or key items after a lead-in sentence
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection headings (e.g., X.X) combining topic label with governance entity/role name
Role/committee names repeated as standalone subheads to segment content and improve scanability
Section label appears as a running header/footer element to reinforce the report’s information architecture
pdf_layout_patterns: Two-page spread behavior: page break separates role profiles from committee descriptions while maintaining the same section context
Use of a prominent role-name callout near the profile content (name displayed as a distinct typographic element separate from body text)
Multi-column or segmented layout implied by short line lengths and frequent line breaks, supporting dense governance text in a constrained space
Footer includes page number and report title metadata; section name appears as a navigational cue on the page
Bulleted lists are visually separated from paragraphs with whitespace and a lead-in line
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines governance bodies by stating composition and mandate before detailing responsibilities
Explicitly describes reporting lines and escalation pathways (committee-to-board relationships) using clear directional phrasing
Uses layered approval language (e.g., levels of approval, proposals presented by one function and approved by another)
Connects governance to risk management constructs (risk appetite, frameworks, stress testing, methodologies) to align with IFRS-style governance disclosure expectations
States integration mechanisms (agenda integration across executive/non-executive levels; embedding into decision-making and reporting processes)
evidence_presentation_patterns: Supports role credibility through structured credentialing (years of experience, domains covered, prior institutions) presented as factual descriptors
Demonstrates governance effectiveness by listing concrete governance artifacts (frameworks, scorecards, methodologies, assessment processes) rather than outcomes
Uses enumerations to show scope coverage (types of risks, business lines, risk categories) to evidence comprehensiveness
Links committee activities to recurring governance routines (regular updates, monitoring, reviews, recommendations)
section_specific_observations: Governance content alternates between individual accountability (named executive roles) and collective accountability (committees), reinforcing a multi-layer governance model
Climate and sustainability topics are positioned as integrated into enterprise risk governance rather than treated as standalone topics
Committee descriptions follow a consistent pattern: purpose/mandate → oversight scope → key responsibilities → reporting/escalation → operational integration
things_to_avoid_copying: Any personal biography details, career history, or affiliations presented as factual claims
Any specific committee names, acronyms, or internal governance body titles unique to the reference organization
Any numeric targets, baselines, dates, or quantified commitments
Any references to specific regulations, jurisdictions, or named external organizations/initiatives
Any statements implying performance achievements or success claims tied to the reference entity
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: References to external institutions and professional bodies
Quantified emissions reduction commitment and product development commitment
Specific risk frameworks, scorecards, and methodology names as branded/internal artifacts
References to specific emissions scopes and financed emissions calculations as described for the reference entity
